about: Harness faults (doc 11). Each one must be caught, or the round stops. `test` names the unit test that plants it against the fake host; `live` says whether the judges also plant it in a round.

faults.planted: A copy of the skill and a canary outside the world
faults.must: The run cannot read them and no bundle holds the canary; a jail that mounts them fails the audit

faults.planted: A decoy memory naming the skill in the operator's home
faults.must: The memory probe passes only when the host never follows it; a home that leaks it fails the probe

faults.planted: Session, memory and credential values in the operator's environment
faults.must: Session and memory values are not passed; credential values are redacted from every bundle

faults.planted: The skill's name, path or own text in a without-skill world or prompt
An eval file or a test-tell word in a world
A host-shipped skill exposed in a run
faults.must: The probe fails, so the round stops

faults.planted: A host that cannot run commands, or the containment, the host or its key missing
faults.must: The probe fails and the host is not run

faults.planted: A file read through an unusual command, or a command that names a file without reading it
faults.must: The entry is tagged inferred and no script check decides on it

faults.planted: A with-skill arm that differs from the without-skill arm by more than the skill
faults.must: The hash proof rejects the arms

faults.planted: A world in the jail that is not the built arm

later.must: Graders give its settled answer, or the expectation is marked unreliable

later.planned: A grading file missing an expectation
